name: @w6w-apps/groq
description: Fast LLM inference, speech and batch processing via Groq's OpenAI-compatible API.

w6w.longDescription:
Groq runs open-weight models (Llama, Qwen, GPT-OSS, Kimi, Whisper, and its own Compound agentic models) on purpose-built LPU hardware, exposed through an OpenAI-compatible surface under `/openai/v1` rather than OpenAI's own `/v1` — the appeal is inference speed and cost, not a different model catalog.

Chat completions cover the core case, including Groq-specific controls with no OpenAI equivalent: a `service_tier` latency/availability trade-off (`flex` fails fast instead of queueing), per-model reasoning-effort and reasoning-format controls for the reasoning models, and Compound-model web search / custom tool configuration. A handful of OpenAI-shaped chat parameters (`frequency_penalty`, `logprobs`, `logit_bias`, and anything beyond `n=1`) are accepted but documented as having no effect on any current model, so this app leaves them out rather than exposing dead controls.

Whisper covers audio transcription and translation, with a Groq-specific convenience OpenAI's own endpoint lacks: either a base64 file OR a plain URL (including a data URL) can be sent in the same request. Text-to-speech, the Batch API (chat-completions requests only, processed over a 24h-7d window against a purpose-built `batch` file upload — Groq's Files API exists only to feed batches, unlike OpenAI's multi-purpose one), and the newer, intentionally stateless Responses (beta) endpoint round out the surface. Embeddings, reranking and fine-tuning appear in Groq's raw API schema but have no documentation page as of writing and are left out entirely rather than guessed at.

A fit for any workflow step that wants an LLM call — especially one where response latency matters more than picking a specific frontier model.
